contents.name: Remark 2.49: maximum over irreducible components
contents.support: Milne §2m 2.49 (printed p.54; PDF p.53) states the maximum-over-irreducible-components formula. The finite closed-cover form uses the recorded direct chain argument: every irreducible closed subset of a finite closed union lies in one cover member.

contents.name: Remark 2.50: dimension of proper closed subsets
contents.support: Finite-dimensional irreducible classical spaces; do not extend the singleton assertion to arbitrary non-T1 spaces.

contents.name: Definition 2.51 and following paragraph: dimension and coordinate rings
Example 3.46: cone plane requires two equations despite codimension one
contents.reason: The scaffold gives this cone as a failure of the ambient intersection bound. The separate arithmetical-rank obstruction needs a divisor or ideal-generation argument and is not used by that calculation.

contents.name: Corollary 3.47: component cut out by codimension-many equations
contents.reason: The algebraic converse height theorem already supplies the local parameter application here; the stronger global component-selection formulation belongs with that supplier.

contents.name: Remark 3.49: factoriality, codimension-one equations, cone planes
contents.reason: The UFD-to-principal-divisor criterion belongs to the divisor interface. Only the explicit cone-plane dimension calculation is used here, harvested separately at Remark 5.37(b).

contents.name: §5j Dimension: function field and affine-open conventions
§5j: dimension of a nonirreducible variety and pure dimension
Proposition 5.36: affine intersection
contents.support: Use irreducible factors, as required by the product argument.

contents.name: Remark 5.37(a): real cone-plane intersection
contents.reason: The page fixes algebraically closed k; the real-locus contrast explains that boundary but is not a claim in its category.

contents.name: §5l Rational maps: definition and equivalence relation
contents.reason: The earlier rational-map interface supplies this definition; this page only transports it between affine charts.

contents.name: Proposition 5.38: field inclusion gives dominant rational map
contents.reason: The established affine correspondence is the supplier for birational comparisons here. The general rational-map construction belongs with that interface rather than being duplicated as a dimension theorem.

contents.name: Corollary 5.39: birational iff function fields isomorphic
Proposition 5.40: birational hypersurface model
contents.reason: The hypersurface model uses a primitive-element presentation and is unnecessary for dimension invariance, which follows directly from common opens.

contents.name: §5m Tangent spaces to varieties; 5.41 tangent/cotangent duality
contents.reason: Tangent and cotangent definitions are the next geometry page; the present dimension proofs use heights and normalization.

contents.name: 5.42: nonsingular iff regular local ring; singular locus closed
contents.reason: Regularity and the singular-locus theorem need the tangent/Jacobian development assigned to that page.

contents.name: 5.43: nonsingular variety
contents.reason: This terminology is introduced alongside the smooth-point criterion, not used by any fibre bound here.

contents.name: §6p Intersections in projective space: Theorem 6.43
contents.support: This is the §6p theorem on printed p.156, not the earlier repeated number.

contents.name: Proposition 6.45: codimension-r projective subvariety is a component of r equations
contents.reason: This homogeneous analogue of the converse height theorem is not needed for the intersection lower bound; retain as a geometric application for the height supplier.

contents.name: Proposition 6.46: pure codimension one in projective space is principal
contents.reason: This classifies projective hypersurfaces via factoriality; the page proves dimension of a given hypersurface and does not need the converse classification.

contents.name: Lemma 6.49: simultaneous hyperplane avoidance
contents.support: Include the elementary product-of-linear-forms argument over infinite k.

contents.name: Remark after 6.49: projection finite; line bundles on punctured affine space
contents.reason: Finite linear projection is flagged for the later finite-map treatment; the asserted triviality of line bundles would require a Picard-group argument not used here.

contents.name: Corollary 6.50: maps P^n to P^m with m<n are constant
contents.reason: Its homogeneous-coordinate presentation uses the preceding unproved line-bundle triviality; this mapping classification is outside the dimension/fibre statements and is not an input.

contents.name: §6q The topology on V times P^n: Lemma 6.51(a)–(c)
contents.support: Read the subsection and full lemma proof. Homogeneous ideals and irrelevant-ideal emptiness; extend affine base to reducible using the same coordinate-ring argument.

contents.name: §7c Theorem 7.22: projective space is complete
contents.support: Only this theorem and proof, pp.164–165: finite graded piece plus Nakayama proves closed projection.

contents.name: Lemma 8.19: finiteness local on the target
contents.reason: The current counterexample needs only the affine module criterion. Global finite-map locality and its affine-preimage condition belong to the morphism interface.

contents.name: Proposition 8.28: finite maps are quasi-finite
contents.support: Scaffold the affine case; global case follows by the deferred locality interface.

contents.name: Lemma 8.29: finite k-algebra has finitely many maximal ideals
Chapter 9 introduction: image of (x,y) maps to (x,xy)
Example 9.2: specialization retaining leading coefficient
contents.support: Use the monic-normalization special case; algebraic closedness supplies roots.

contents.name: Lemma 9.3: one-generator extension avoiding a chosen element
contents.reason: This is an alternative generator-induction proof of the open-image lemma. The selected proof clears monic normalization denominators instead; no arbitrary-polynomial specialization is needed.

contents.name: Lemma 9.4: extension avoiding a nonzero element
contents.reason: The localization-and-normalization proof gives the needed image open directly. This stronger element-avoidance formulation is not a missing prerequisite of that route.

contents.name: Aside 9.5: generic flatness alternative
contents.reason: Generic flatness is an alternative proof of dominance-open-image, not the chosen denominator-clearing route.

contents.name: Constructible subsets: definition, unions, intersections, complements
Proposition 9.6: dense constructible set contains open
Theorem 9.7: image of a constructible set is constructible
Aside 9.8: complex closure equals Zariski closure
contents.reason: The complex analytic topology comparison is not available over arbitrary algebraically closed fields and is not needed for Chevalley.

contents.name: §9b The fibres of a regular map: Theorem 9.9(a)
Theorem 9.9(b): lower bound and generic equality
contents.support: Lower bound has its own carrier thm-fibre-dimension-lower-bound. Replace the printed generic proof by Vakil normalization and use nonempty fibres only.

contents.name: Theorem 9.9(c): claimed closed jump loci
contents.support: Qualification essential: retain target semicontinuity only for projective morphisms, independently verified by Vakil Class 38 Exercise 3.B. The unrestricted printed assertion is not used.

contents.name: Example 9.10: linear systems and rank loci
contents.support: Keep fibre n-rank and minors; do not assume the total solution variety irreducible or copy its unjustified global dimension formula.

contents.name: Proposition 9.11: closed map with irreducible equidimensional fibres
Warning after Proposition 9.11: x1^2 y1-x2^2 y2 and reducible fibres
contents.reason: The printed assertion about all fibres being reducible has exceptional coefficient choices and characteristic qualifications. The general warning is retained in rem-equidimensionality-hypotheses; this inaccurate specific assertion is not relied on.

contents.name: §3c Note 3.13: components through a point and minimal primes in its local ring
contents.support: Explains the component-through-point convention; local ring equality for irreducible X is proved separately using the height supplier.

contents.name: Corollary 4.1.7: regular-sequence dimension drop
